card: Fixes wallet accounting in gettransaction, listtransactions, and listsinceblock for mixed-input transactions such as CoinJoins and Payjoins. Currently, the wallet assumes all inputs are wallet-owned, resulting in fabricated recipient send entries and incorrect or negative fee reporting (issue #14136). The PR replaces this speculation with a conservative fallback that reports an unattributed aggregate send debit and omits fees unless non-wallet inputs are known zero-value outputs (such as ephemeral anchors). It also adds involves_mixed_inputs, wallet_debit, and wallet_credit fields to RPC output entries.
changed_since_previous: The approach and functionality are unchanged; changes since the previous version are minor rebasing and test/documentation polish.
evidence: Addresses long-standing issue #14136 ('rpc: Wrong `gettransaction` info for a coinjoin'), open since 2018.

Existing functional test comments in test/functional/wallet_listtransactions.py previously asserted incorrect fee accounting: 'Fee should be correct... But it is not, see for example https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/14136'.
problem: When a wallet transaction spends both wallet-owned and external inputs, wallet history RPCs assume all inputs belong to the wallet. This fabricates false recipient send entries and produces incorrect or even negative fee figures, a problem that is particularly noticeable and unavoidable when rescanning the chain or importing descriptors without local transaction metadata.

risk.why: A mistake in transaction input classification or caching could corrupt wallet debit/credit calculations or break external software that relies on the schema of wallet history RPCs.

scope_notes: Adds a large new functional test suite in test/functional/wallet_gettransaction_mixed_inputs.py (+700 lines) covering CoinJoin and anchor input scenarios, reorganizations, and descriptor imports.
summary: Classifies transaction input ownership in wallet accounting helpers and updates history RPCs (gettransaction, listtransactions, listsinceblock) for mixed-input transactions such as CoinJoins and Payjoins. When foreign inputs have unknown or non-zero value, these RPCs report a single unattributed aggregate send debit with no fee or recipient address, alongside normal receive entries for wallet-owned outputs. When foreign inputs are verified zero-value (such as PayToAnchor outputs), standard per-output send and fee attribution is preserved, and new metadata fields (involves_mixed_inputs, wallet_debit, wallet_credit) are exposed.
